handoff: review#1: approve. Spec and standards checked: B54, B56-B60 on run view/list, D2 interaction + FakeInteraction; AC1-AC6 tested in targets.test.ts, AC7 hand-checked by implement. bun test packages/cli 345 pass, typecheck clean. Non-blocking: B57 order test mirrors the impl (recheck after slice 04 status change), for-await over stdin may break a second prompt in one process (later D2 prompts), hasRun loads a run view per unit, a redundant wrapper.

findings.title: The status-order test rebuilds its expected order the same way the code does
findings.detail:
The B57 test builds the expected order as inbox items followed by stories with their slices. That is the same algorithm as unitsInStatusOrder in runtime/target.ts, so a wrong idea of 'status order' would pass in both places. Today `norn status` prints stories only. Inbox-first status is slice 04 (B9). The implementation follows where status is going, which is a reasonable reading.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Once slice 04 lands, assert the pick-list order against the order of units in `norn status` output, or against a literal list for this fixture.

findings.title: Returning from `for await` over process.stdin can end the stream for later prompts
findings.detail:
pick() returns from inside `for await (const chunk of stdin)`. That calls the iterator's return(), which in Node-compatible streams destroys the readable. One prompt per process works today. D2's confirm, ask-a-line and edit prompts (later slices) may chain a second prompt after a pick in the same process, and it would get no input.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: When a second prompt is added, read keys with a 'data' listener that is removed in finally, instead of async iteration.

findings.title: hasRun loads a full run view for every unit
findings.detail:
applies() calls loadRunView for each candidate just to test for a run, which reads receipts and state per unit. The cost is O(units) file reads on every command without a target. It is fine at current sizes.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Decide from the ProjectView that was already loaded (view.runs, or each unit's run state), if it carries enough.

findings.title: Wrapper that only forwards its argument
findings.detail:
`command: (key) => command(key)` just passes `command` through.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: `command,`
